basis: Cutaneous hamartoma composed of eccrine sweat glands and proliferating capillary vessels.
Cardiac and skeletal abnormalities define the syndrome; ptosis in 20/23 (~87%) and intellectual disability in 8/23 (~35%) support ocular and neurologic involvement.
Cerebral motor injury causes bilateral lower-limb spasticity; muscle hypertonia alone does not establish primary muscle disease.
Benign epithelial neoplasm arising from gastric pyloric glands.
Benign mesothelial neoplasm arising from the peritoneal lining of the abdominal cavity.
Defined by cardiac disease together with abnormalities of skin or hair.
Tooth agenesis and nail dysplasia are defining, nearly universal features; teeth belong to gastrointestinal and nails to dermatologic.
Ovarian dysgenesis causes endocrine failure: low estradiol and elevated FSH in 3/3. Short stature and delayed maturation do not establish skeletal damage.
Inherited early-onset Alzheimer disease causes progressive cerebral neurodegeneration and dementia.
Mechanical impairment of eyelid closure is an eyelid disorder.
Congenital retinal dystrophy causes visual impairment, retinal degeneration and optic disc pallor; optic nerve findings remain ocular.
Defined by immune dysregulation and immunodeficiency with severe infantile bowel inflammation and arthritis; infections and lymphoma risk add no organ axes.
Inherited glomerular basement membrane disease. Subtype-specific hearing loss is only 5–29% (1/7); ocular damage is rare, despite the generic Alport definition.
Benign placental neoplasm is confined to an obstetric organ outside the axes.
Combined T- and B-cell functional immunodeficiency; pneumonia, despite occurring in 2/2 reported patients, is a separately diagnosed infection.
Malignancy of the reproductive testis; no endocrine origin or hormone dysfunction is specified.
Urothelial carcinoma arises in the ureter, which belongs to the renal axis.
Congenital pituitary growth hormone deficiency causes severe growth failure; short stature and delayed skeletal maturation alone do not establish skeletal damage.
Malignant neoplasm of vascular endothelial cells; no specific skin or visceral site is established.
Skeletal dysplasia with platyspondyly, rhizomelia and kyphosis. Blue sclerae in 1/3 do not establish ocular functional damage; feeding difficulty is a symptom.
Primary skeletal myopathy with proximal weakness and focal mitochondrial depletion; no separate systemic metabolic or neurologic disorder is established.
Developmental overgrowth of lower-limb bones and soft tissues defines the disorder; optional vascular abnormalities lack evidence of a frequency of at least 30%.
Glycogen branching enzyme deficiency with childhood skeletal myopathy. Cardiomyopathy is variable; a ≥30% frequency is uncertain. Hepatic forms are distinct.
Thiamine metabolism/transport disorder defined by developmental impairment, seizures and progressive brain injury; respiratory insufficiency occurs in only 5–29%.
Iris pigment shedding and deposition occur within the eye; subsequent pigmentary glaucoma is a separate ocular diagnosis and adds no axis.
